chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abu al-Maghra', from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performs *zihar* with his wife, then intends to complete the divorce upon her. He said: There is no expiation upon him. I said: If he intends to have intercourse with her? He said: He should not have intercourse with her until he expiates. I said: If he does so, is there something upon him? He said: By Allah, he is sinful and unjust. I said: Is there upon him an expiation other than the first one? He said: Yes, he frees a slave.

key_terms.يَمَسَّهَا: To have intercourse (literally: to touch her)
key_terms.يُظَاهِرُ: Performs zihar (declaring wife like mother's back)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man performs zihar and then has intercourse with his wife before completing the expiation?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the specific legal nuance of *Zihar* by distinguishing between the initial expiation for the declaration and the penalty for consummating intercourse before its completion. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes that premature intimacy renders the husband sinful and unjust (*thamin zalim*), necessitating a second expiation, thereby reinforcing the procedural integrity of the divorce process in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling highlights the transition from the pre-Islamic practice to a structured, expiation-based system that protects the wife's status during the waiting period.
